| VRSQ oculomotor (0–100) | 25.0 | — | 8.3 | 0.0 | 11.1 |
| VRSQ disorientation (0–100) | 13.3 | — | 0.0 | 0.0 | 4.4 |
| VRSQ total (0–100) | 19.2 | — | 4.2 | 0.0 | 7.8 |

UEQ-S: pragmatic = items 1–4, hedonic = items 5–8 (Schrepp et al., 2017). VRSQ: oculomotor = items 1–4 ÷ 12 × 100, disorientation = items 5–9 ÷ 15 × 100, total = their mean (Kim et al., 2018). A participant with any item missing gets no score.

## Five design principles — evidence from the session

The brief asks for an evaluation against the five principles (Week 6), including any that do not apply. Observer notes were not logged live, so "facilitator recall" below is Kaike's account after the session — no counts.

| Principle | Evidence logged | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Text readability | Facilitator recall: **nobody squinted** or leaned in to read. The design carries almost no text (cards are colour only; three large frame labels) | **Met** |
| Ergonomics | No observation recorded (arm held up, crouching). Logged: furniture placed where meant first try 2 / 4 (P2, P3) | **Not evaluated** — no evidence either way beyond row 14 |
| Brightness changes | VRSQ eyestrain (item 3): 1 slight (P1), none for P2–P4. No observation recorded of reactions to the curtains closing | **No problem indicated** by VRSQ; not observed directly |
| Avoiding simulator sickness | Facilitator recall: **no one reported sickness**. VRSQ total mean 7.8 / 100, highest 19.2 (P1); P2 incomplete. Teleport only, no smooth locomotion | **Met** |
| Button placement | Facilitator recall: **some participants got stuck holding the ball** (number not logged). Row 22: 3 / 4 named "the ball" as the most confusing thing; row 20 (P4): "confusing the way you pick the ball". The sample stays in the hand with no button held, and letting go means squeezing and releasing the grip — nothing in the scene shows that | **Not met** for releasing a sample — the main usability finding |

## Data quality — read before quoting any of this

- **n = 4**, below the target of 5. All four on the studio Meta Quest 3S (`…L04R5`) with controllers. The first studio headset (`…G6M009N`) never authorised USB debugging (UQ-managed), so it was swapped at 13:57; the app first ran on the headset at 14:03.
- **Phase timers were not used**: every prompt is logged as "task 1". Which prompts were used is usable; their phase and order are not.
- **Row 5 (time to first commit) was not recorded** for anyone (stopwatch not started).
- **Rows 8a / 8b (hold-up / toss tallies) are identical for every participant** (1/1, 0/0, 1/1, 4/4). Possibly both counters were tapped together; treat the B3 commit split as unreliable. Row 20 (verbatim) is the better B3 evidence.
- **No app event log to cross-check B3**: nobody consented to recording, so `record-session.sh` (which also captures the app log) was not run. The headset's main log buffer is 256 KiB and had rolled over by export (15:47), so no commit lines survive. `device/app-events-2026-10-23.txt` holds only the system log's 7 launches of the app (13:57–15:07, including relaunches by the facilitator) and **no crash or death of the app process** since 13:57.
- **Observer notes are empty for all four**: the B3 step-back / overview question (added 23 Oct) and the five-principles observations were not logged.
- P2's VRSQ is incomplete (missing: v6), so P2 has no VRSQ score.
- P4 had seen the project before.
- Verbatims are as typed on the iPad (spelling unchanged).
